reviewText: A superhero epic of gargantuan proportions that overwhelms and overstimulates, but still manages to deliver some human emotions despite the CGI circus.
This time, it's the audience that gets... TAKEN.
It's how I'd imagine an over-caffeinated Tony Scott would shoot a Transformer-less Transformers film.
Taken 3 makes Taken 2 look like Taken.
The post-Endgame MCU continues to be a slog.
Not as much fun as it should have been, but still enjoyable in its own cheesy way.

This is my kind of family-focused relationship light drama and fun, and it helps that the wider picture of where the MCU is heading finally starts to come into focus. QUANTUMANIA is an ant-astic return to form for Marvel after a few lackluster entries.
In the case of the third Ant-Man movie, bigger does mean better, but not without a few growing pains.
Taken 3 is such a blatant paycheque gig for Liam Neeson, you almost expect him to stop midmovie to deposit his loot into an ATM.

Mildly competent and mostly diverting, but the formula is getting stale, and it feels like everyone involved knows it. These characters deserve a break, and so does this increasingly preposterous, threadbare series.

It's nice Hollywood's been scouring metaphysical and cosmological texts and translating them into comic book popcorn entertainment (The Quantum Realm!) but the over-usage of CGI as a lazy replacement for the craft of good storytelling is tedious.
Marvel today is an amusement park, expanding, building new rides and attractions, trying, flailing and failing to recapture the magic of the past decade.
The whole thing seems to be built almost entirely on cliches and tropes, with no gravity, no sense of impact or consequence.
The future of the MCU is as uncertain as ever, but “Quantumania” has the train back up on the tracks and (hopefully) headed in the right direction.
A stinker.

ANT-MAN & THE WASP: Quantumania feels more like a Disney+ special than a film.

It’s messy, overindulgent on weak CGI, and humor falls flat. Jonathan Majors is great as Kang but Marvel seemed more focused on creating a 2-hour trailer for something better.
Despite strong performances from the cast, 'Quantumania' is dull and exhausting to sit through. Marvel’s glory days might be behind us and I’m really not looking forward to the rest of Phase Five.
Everyone involved with this picture should be embarrassed, and boy do they look it.
If you've seen Taken or Taken 2, you've already been taken, and there's not much different here.
Unfortunately, Taken 3 will be remembered as the one where Neeson just couldn't save the day.
Taken with no one taken? That would be like The Exorcist with no exorcist. Cabin in the Woods with no cabin in the woods. Nightmare on Elm Street with no nightmares.
This is another entry that fails to muster excitement or move things forward in a meaningful way. It just exists – a gear in a moneymaking machine that is starting to lose its steam.
A return to what Marvel does best ... teasing the next movie.

The film is strictly made for die-hard Marvel and Ant-Man fans. Watch it for its special effects and imaginatively constructed landscape and creatures. Don’t go looking for drama and you won’t be disappointed.
Seven years on, and with three episodes of The Expendables leaving the geri-action flick well and truly spent, Taken 3 feels as dozy as a pensioner in the midday sun.
Quantunmania is colorful, original, and different, and corrects the mistakes that Marvel has made during these three years of experimentation. [Full review in Spanish]
Nothing gets taken here except your ticket money.
For a franchise in need of refreshment, it’s anything but a quantum leap.
This film is impossible to take seriously, but never makes the mistake of doing so itself, and as a consequence is perfectly watchable.
It's Neeson that franchise fans will come back for. And although his lethally protective father routine has run its course, it's been fun watching the old bloke make the most of it.
...a sequel that's right in line with its immediate predecessor...
Its hilarious, mind-bendingly stupid climax is nearly worth the price of admission alone.
